Ranges are commonly cited values; the user can always correct them in the form. | grind calibration points (calibPoints/uniformity, P0) merged in. | espresso brewers carry pressureRegime (fixed pump vs. variable/piloted). | v11-13 (13 supersedes both sides' 11): every calibration point used to sit in the FILTER range (400-1300 um), so where espresso falls on a dial could only be extrapolated, and drifted. Each espresso-capable grinder now carries an ESPRESSO anchor at 250 um (the centre of the 200-300 um window), placed at the centre of its published espresso setting range - from the maker's own microns-per-click where there is one (1Zpresso, Weber), else from published/community setting ranges. A window a grinder reaches only partly is CLIPPED to what it reaches, not refused - nearly every grinder, filter ones included, goes fine enough for a turbo/soup shot. Silence is reserved for a window lying entirely off the dial (a filter-only grinder asked about espresso). | v12: baskets join the catalog (kind "basket", basketStyle + basketDoseGrams) so they are picked like papers instead of typed. A basket is a sub-item of the MACHINE and is never a lever - it only moves where the espresso grind zone sits. | v14: the grinder catalog grows again - the Femobook line, the Eureka Mignon family, and a batch of hand and electric grinders across brands. Truly stepless dials whose zero is set at assembly and differs per unit (Eureka Mignon, Option-O Remi, Mazzer Philos, Fiorenzato F64 Evo) carry no calibPoints - their printed numbers are personal to each grinder, never a cross-grinder translation. | v15: a new kind "burrs" (burrDiameterMm, burrGeometry, uniformity as the character these meules give - no adjustment range, no calibPoints: swapping burrs moves the zero and breaks the grinder's own curve) with 7 aftermarket sets (SSP MP/HU/Cast/Brew at 64 and 98mm, DLC-coated 64mm, Option-O Mizen ES). A set only earns an entry if it can actually be fitted to ANOTHER grinder: a grinder's own proprietary burrs are not a choice and would only cost their owner a curve. Conversely a few grinders LEAVE THE FACTORY on a set listed here (Fellow Ode Gen 2 on SSP MPs, Lagom P64 on Mizens), so they carry stockBurrsFamilies: naming those describes the grinder instead of re-burring it, and its curve - measured with them in - holds. Grinder iteration hygiene: the missing "Turin DF64 (Gen 1)" entry joins with its OWN stock-burr curve (the bare "df64" alias stayed on Gen 2 only, to not silently re-point already-synced saved gear - each generation now also carries its own specific alias, e.g. "df64 gen1"/"df64 gen 2"); the existing "DF64 / + SSP Multipurpose" entry keeps its id, aliases and measured curve untouched (only its notes gained a cross-reference); Comandante C40 MK3 is now a same-curve alias of the MK4 entry (identical burrs, cosmetic revision only). | v16: the grinder catalog widens again across brands - 1Zpresso K-Plus/K-Pro, Kingrinder K3/K5/K7, Timemore Chestnut Slim/X/G1/Nano, Hario Skerton Plus, Porlex Tall, Made By Knock Feldgrind, Normcore V3, VSSL Java, Sage Dose Control Pro, Rancilio Rocky, Gaggia MDF, Melitta Calibra, Krups GX5000, De'Longhi Dedica KG521 and KG79, Baratza Sette 30 and Forte, Eureka Atom and Zenith 65E, Fiorenzato F4 Nano, Mahlkönig E65S, Turin DF83, Varia VS6, Niche Duo, Capresso Infinity, Cuisinart DBM-8 and OXO Brew Conical Burr. Where a model shares its maker's own confirmed burr, click count and micron span with an already-catalogued sibling (1Zpresso K-Max for K-Plus/K-Pro, Kingrinder K2 for K3/K5, Baratza Vario+ for Forte), it reuses that measured curve rather than inventing a new one. Ceado, Compak, Macap, Anfim, Solis, Graef, Weber Key Mk1 and Hario Mini Mill Plus were checked and left out for lack of a specific, source-backed espresso or filter reference point. | v18 (2026-09-06, CUP-132): an electric filter machine is a batchBrewer ONLY when it is one-button (the machine heats, pours and times on its own: Moccamaster, Ratio, Bonavita, Wilfa). A PROGRAMMABLE machine, where the user sets the bloom, the pours and the temperature (Fellow Aiden, xBloom, Breville Precision Brewer), is declared pourOver: its recipe has the manual-filter structure, exactly like the OXO Rapid Brewer precedent. Fellow Aiden and xBloom added. | v19 (2026-09-08, CUP-165): the method label is gone. Every brewer declares a STRUCTURE instead - the shape of the recipe it takes, which is the one thing every screen and every lever needed: manual (bloom, pours in grams, pour style; the valve hybrids Clever/Switch/Bonavita Immersion Dripper are here, their valve gestures ride in each step's note), programmed (same structure, the user programs it: Fellow Aiden, xBloom, Breville Precision Brewer), reservoir (bloom and pours in grams, no pour style: OXO Rapid Brewer, AeroPress, Delter, Tricolate, NextLevel Pulsar), immersion (dose, water, temperature, a steeping rest: French press, Espro, and provisionally the siphons until they get their own descriptor), electricFilter (one-button machines: Moccamaster, Wilfa Svart Performance, Ratio Six/Eight, Bonavita Connoisseur), espresso, moka (dose and water weighed, no temperature lever) and cold (ratio, grind, hours). A brewer the catalog does not know picks its structure in its own form. | v19 (suite, 09/09/2026, CUP-165, decision d'Arthur) : une entree cafetiere peut porter tempBand [min, max], la fenetre de temperature de CETTE cafetiere. Une entree peut aussi refuser le STYLE de versement avec pourStyle false : le NextLevel Pulsar est un filtre manuel a valve, ses impulsions restent des versements en quantites, mais la facon de poser l'eau n'y decide rien. | v20 (2026-09-14, CUP-210) : une entree cafetiere espresso porte temperatureAdjustable, le seul fait qui dise si la temperature d'eau se REGLE sur cette machine. Les cadrans en MICRONS (EK Omnia, Zerno Z1) mesurent un ecart de meules, pas une taille de particule : ils n'ont donc AUCUN calibPoint, l'app porte le bon cadran et refuse de le traduire plutot que d'inventer une courbe. La 98 MP a ete corrigee : elle pretendait etre vendue aussi sous le nom LU, ce qui est faux (SSP vend MP, HU, LU, ULU et Sweet Lab comme cinq produits distincts a cette taille), donc ses alias "ssp lu" sont passes a la nouvelle entree Low Uniformity 98 mm. Un champ absent vaut mieux qu'un chiffre estime. | v25 (2026-09-20, CUP-280, decision d'Arthur) : le DIXIEME devient un fait du catalogue. Classement, un moulin a la fois et jamais au jugement : FAUX pour toute unite en clics (un cran est un cran) et pour les cadrans deja en microns ; FAUX pour les bagues crantees que les notes decrivent comme telles (Baratza Virtuoso+/Sette/Vario/Forte, dont seule la bague MACRO est modelisee, EG-1 en pas de 5 um, et les petits electriques a N positions) ; VRAI pour les 1Zpresso, dont l'echelle EST une notation numero.clic, et pour les moulins dont les notes disent sans fin avec une echelle chiffree imprimee. Le 1Zpresso 'Q2 Heptagonal' prend son nom commercial 'Q2 S' (1Zpresso range Q2, Q2 S et Q sur une meme fiche produit, meme reglage de 30 clics par tour ; la courbe mesuree ne change pas) et garde 'q2 heptagonal' en alias pour que le materiel deja enregistre se resynchronise. Regle stricte : allround seulement si les sources disent que le moulin fait BIEN les deux ; un moulin qui atteint l'espresso mais y est mediocre est filter (Comandante C40, Fellow Ode, Baratza Encore, EK43), un moulin a doseur mediocre en filtre est espresso (Rancilio Rocky, Gaggia MDF). Hesitations tranchees : 1Zpresso J-Ultra espresso (page fabricant), Sage Smart Grinder Pro allround (revues independantes contre la note du catalogue), EK43 S filter (comme l'EK43, malgre le 'Allround Shop Grinder' recent de Mahlkonig), Timemore Nano allround. Sans moulin designe pour une famille, l'app choisit le moulin concu pour elle, un allround ensuite, et en espresso un electrique a conception egale. Le catalogue DISTANT doit porter ces deux champs a partir de v32, sinon il masquerait l'embarque. | v33 (2026-09-24, CUP-346, decision d'Arthur du 23/09 : qu'un materiel absent soit ultra rare) : une FICHE D'IDENTITE est admise seule. Elle porte le type, la marque, le modele, la structure de recette pour une cafetiere, et un champ source : la page du fabricant (a defaut, d'un revendeur) qui etablit le produit sous ce nom. Plage, courbe, microns, regime de pression et temperature reglable restent optionnels, chacun source, et ne s'ajoutent qu'une fois etablis. Une fiche sans aucun fait au-dela de son identite (moulin sans plage, machine espresso sans regime, fiche sans notes) doit porter sa source ; verify.sh le controle. Un moulin reconnu sans plage ni courbe se comporte comme un moulin inconnu : aucune plage n'est inventee, la mouture du plan reste en mots, et la fiche Materiel demande les deux extremites puis un reglage de reference en dernier recours. Recherche complete, confiance basse comprise, et physique agitation x fines : docs/catalog-sources/grinder-fines-v34.json et agitation-fines-physics.md. Champ vide = on ne sait pas, jamais 'peu de fines'. Le champ uniformity n'est PAS corrige ici malgre cinq contradictions relevees (C2, Forte, Mini Mill Slim+, J-Ultra, Skerton).

Cone dripper paired with a flow-distribution waterspout insert for even, hands-off water dispersion.
Ceramic cone with internal ribs and a slightly shallower angle; even, balanced extraction.

Double-wall steel dripper with ridged walls; BOTH X and XF are flat-bottom, steep-walled baskets (Fellow's own "Stagg X Dripper" product page; nucleuscoffee.com, "Fellow Stagg X Brewer Review — The Best Flat Bottom Dripper?"; coffeeadastra.com) — only their SIZE differs, not the geometry (corrected 2026-09-21, CUP-291; this note used to say X was conical). Heat-retentive, even bed, ratio markings inside.
Scandinavian competition-favorite flat-bottom brewer (Patrik Rolf); large single drain, fast flow, clean repeatable comp-style brews.
Flat-floor brewer with a very open base; extremely fast drawdown. V4 is modular with interchangeable bottoms. Competition staple.

OREA's small unibody flat-bottom brewer ('Baby O'), open bottom with a ridge supporting the filter. Size 155 papers (Wave 155, OREA Flat small, Sibarist FAST small); built for 10-18 g of coffee (160-300 ml). Tritan or stainless steel. Source: orea.uk/o1-brewer, read 2026-09-23.
Reference flat-bottom 3-hole brewer; forgiving, even extraction, wavy filter stabilizes the bed.
Minimalist single-hole flat-bottom ceramic; slow controlled flow for sweet, balanced cups.
Original zero-bypass flat-bed brewer with stepless flow-control valve; impermeable walls force all water through the bed.
Flat-bottom immersion/percolation hybrid with shower screen and stepless valve (Jonathan Gagne collab); clarity-focused, no bypass.
Original wedge single-hole cone; mass-market, easy, the historical pour-over standard.
Flat-bottom immersion brewer with a bottom release valve; steep-then-drain, very forgiving.
Flat-bottom brewer designed with Tim Wendelboe; matched to Wilfa filters for even, comp-grade extraction.
Fast-flowing Kalita-Wave-style ceramic flat-bottom dripper, multi-hole; well-priced, even extraction.
Hourglass carafe using thick bonded paper filters; very slow flow, exceptionally clean, low-body cup.
Plastic cone with a gravity-actuated shut-off valve that opens when set on a mug; near-foolproof immersion-then-drip, paper-clean cup.
Classic steep-and-plunge with a single metal mesh; oils and fines pass through for a heavy, full body.
French press with a patented double micro-filter (basket-in-basket) that traps grit and stops extraction at plunge; much cleaner than a standard press.
Combined immersion plus manual pressure through a paper or metal filter; variants differ only in size/material, not method.

Same combined immersion plus manual pressure method as the standard AeroPress, in a larger chamber (maker-stated 20 oz / ~590 ml, about double the standard AeroPress); own catalog family so its size survives a re-sync instead of being read back as the standard model.
Injection piston press: a Jet-Seal keeps water off the grounds until you press, then injects water through the puck; pour-over-like, avoids true immersion agitation.
Fridge pitcher with a tall mesh filter basket; brews ready-to-drink (not concentrate) cold brew in ~8-12h.
Bucket-style immersion brewer making a strong concentrate (~1:3 to serve) through a felt/paper filter; classic low-acid cold brew, 12-24h.

Compact pressure-assisted brewer: the water is pressed through the bed rather than free-falling, so the brew is a bloom then ONE single pour with all the remaining water, never staged fractional pours. Its rapid cold brew PERCOLATES under pressure too: grind FINER than filter there, never coarse, and the concentrate is meant to be diluted to serve.
SCA/ECBC-certified Dutch-built drip brewer; brews half or full 1.25L carafe to Golden Cup standard.
Simulated-pour-over auto drip; Series 2 added redesigned carafe and reservoir markings.
Walnut-paneled flagship one-button drip brewer; Series 2 refresh.

SCA-certified PROGRAMMABLE drip: adjustable temperature, bloom time and flow rate, so the user sets the recipe the way a hand pourer does. Declared pourOver for that reason (manual-filter structure, temperature a lever), not batchBrewer.

Programmable precision brewer: each profile sets the water temperature, the bloom (ratio and duration) and pulsed pours, single-cup or batch basket. The user writes the recipe, so it reads as a pour-over (bloom, staged pours, temperature a lever), never as a one-button batch brewer.

App-programmable pour-over machine with built-in grinder and scale: every recipe sets the temperature, the bloom, the pour pattern and the pauses. Reads as a pour-over (the user writes the structure), never as a one-button batch brewer.
Tim Wendelboe-designed Norwegian filter machine; holds 92-96C, adjustable flow with steep-and-release.
Single-button thermal-carafe drip brewer.
Borosilicate vacuum pot with alcohol/beam-heater burner (3 and 5-cup); Hario pioneered the format.
Hand-blown glass stovetop/burner vacuum pot (3, 5, 8-cup); long-standing siphon staple.
Taiwanese glass vacuum brewer; same gravity-then-vacuum siphon principle as Hario/Yama.
58mm group manual lever; pour off-boil water and pull by hand, with detachable preheat controller. Current flagship.
Entry-level lever maker with pressurized-style basket; easiest Flair on-ramp.
Die-cast lever press with twin arms; no electricity. Barista version adds an in-basket pressure gauge.
Hand-pumped portable espresso for ground coffee (~18 bar claimed); travel and camping staple.
Compact pro-oriented portable with a naked 52mm 18g basket for true specialty shots on the go.
Twin-lever manual press producing 5-10 bar; Commercial/Pro editions add a gauge.
Prosumer 58mm-portafilter machine with a commercial-style steam wand; a common first upgrade from pod machines.
58mm single-boiler prosumer classic, largely unchanged for two decades; commercial-grade steam wand.
Built-in conical burr grinder, 54mm portafilter and steam wand in one all-in-one machine.

items.notes: Slim 15-bar pump machine with a small single/double portafilter; compact-kitchen staple.
Dual-boiler 58mm machine with a flow-control paddle (pressure profiling) and a PID display.
Heat-exchanger 58mm machine with a flow-control paddle and a PID-controlled brew boiler.
Compact heat-exchanger machine with a copper boiler and E61 group; a popular home upgrade.
Dual-boiler PID machine with an E61 group, built on the same platform as the ECM Synchronika.
Home-sized single-boiler descendant of La Marzocco's commercial Linea, with app-controlled profiling.
Software-driven machine exposing full pressure/flow profiling and shot graphs on its touchscreen.
Classic manual spring-lever machine, hand-pulled shots with no pump or electronics.
Classic stovetop aluminium moka pot; the original moka design.
Pressure-valve moka pot; silicone pressure regulator builds extra pressure for a crema-like layer.
Standard reference paper for V60; slow flow with coffee in the bed, balanced cup.
Standard reference paper for V60 size 01; slow flow with coffee in the bed.
Abaca-fiber cone paper; flows slightly faster than Hario stock, very consistent, crisp cup.
Thicker Abaca; flows like regular Abaca once coffee is in the bed, more clarity.
Thin one-side crepe, high density; clean cup with strong aroma, made for light roasts.
Thick two-side crepe, low density; normal flow with coffee in the bed, a balanced, rich cup. Cafec's MEDIUM-roast paper (T-83 is the dark-roast one).
Two-side low-crepe, medium density; normal flow with coffee in the bed, made to bring out body and sweetness in dark roasts.
Premium fast filter; drains faster than standard papers, so the same bed takes a finer grind without stalling, very clean cup.
Fast flat-bottom filter for Kalita/Orea-style brewers.
Flat-bottom wave paper; normal flow, very even extraction, forgiving.
Very thick bonded paper; slow flow, removes most oils and fines, exceptionally clean cup.
Uses standard V60-style cone papers; medium flow.
40mm conical, espresso-tuned. Max ~820µm (barely reaches filter coarseness); fines-heavy at coarse — better for espresso.

DF64 (Gen1) + SSP Multipurpose 64mm flat. Measured PSD: median µm ≈ 205 + 13.4×dial. Low fines, high clarity. Now also expressible as the catalog's separate "Turin DF64 (Gen 1)" grinder fitted with the standalone "SSP Multi Purpose 64 mm" burrs entry - this entry is kept as-is (own id, aliases and measured curve) so gear already saved against it stays intact.
Precision basket, tightly graded holes and a high open area.

Superfine mesh: the most open there is, flows fastest.
Precision basket.
Precision basket.
The single-wall basket most machines ship with.
Makes its own back-pressure through one small hole; forgiving, and wants a much coarser grind.
Step-down basket: narrows toward the bottom so the same dose sits deeper. Filed under precision (Arthur, 2026-09-03: four readable categories, not five).
38mm conical burr, ~18 microns/click (40 clicks/rotation, ~3 rotations); portable electric spanning moka pot to French press.
38mm conical burr, 8 microns/click (100 clicks/rotation, ~3 rotations); budget dual-purpose for espresso and pour-over.
48mm conical burr sharing the 1Zpresso ZP6 geometry, 8 microns/click; pour-over only, no published espresso range.
53mm heptagonal conical burr, 8 microns/click; handles espresso and pour-over but slow on shots (50-70s per double).
68mm conical burr, 8 microns/click (~3 rotations); large single burr for both espresso and filter, catch cup fits 58mm portafilters.
Read as rotation.number.tick; 10 clicks per number, 100 per rotation, ~4.5 rotations usable, range 0-1230 microns.
38mm circle-ball burr, 18 microns/click, 40 clicks/rotation; pour-over, French press and cold brew only, not built for espresso.
38mm circle-ball burr, 18 microns/click, 40 clicks/rotation; entry-level espresso grinder.
48mm circle-ball burr, 18 microns/click, 40 clicks/rotation; handles espresso through pour-over.
38mm CNC stainless conical burr, ~32 microns/click; bigger-hopper C2 sibling, same click structure as the base C2.
42mm S2C conical burr, 50 clicks/rotation (~15 microns/click), 3 rotations; read as rotation.number.tick, shown here as cumulative clicks.
Ceramic conical burr, 24 clicks/rotation, 350-1400 micron range; not fine enough for consistent espresso - filter and French press only.

Small conical burr, read as rotation.number.tick (cumulative here); handles filter beautifully, espresso works but consistency drops off at the finest settings (more fines mixed with coarse, prone to channeling).
48mm steel conical burr, ~58 microns/click; hand grinder, not recommended past 25 clicks from zero.

Etzinger 48mm ring + 32mm cone burr set; macro dial reads in approximate microns (e.g. '400+10'), plus a separate 5-micron micro disk for espresso fine-tuning layered on top - only the macro dial is modeled here.

78mm/75mm Ghost Tooth burrs; dial reads C-9 (finest) to C+9 (coarsest) around a Center detente, mapped here to 1-19 with Center=10. Pour-over, drip and immersion only - cannot grind fine enough for espresso.
39mm Nitro Blade S2 burr, same burr family as the C40; 40-step travel grinder, particle distribution close to the C40 MK4.

Stepless dial: numbers are arbitrary and differ per unit (the zero is set at assembly) - settings are personal to your grinder, no cross-grinder translation. Covers the whole Mignon line (Specialità, Silenzio, Zero, Manuale, Oro, Perfetto...) which shares the same 50-55mm flat stepless collar (Oro runs 65mm); all variants are espresso-capable.

Stepless dial: numbers are arbitrary and differ per unit - settings are personal to your grinder, no cross-grinder translation. 38mm conical burr set: conventional burrs for drip/press (can't reach espresso) or contemporary burrs for espresso and Turkish.

Stepless dial: numbers are arbitrary and differ per unit - settings are personal to your grinder, no cross-grinder translation. 64mm flat burr single-dose grinder; also offers a stepped 6-micron mode, not modeled here.

Stepless dial: numbers are arbitrary and differ per unit - settings are personal to your grinder, no cross-grinder translation. 64mm flat burr, touchscreen on-demand espresso grinder with no clicks or detents at all.
Macro ring only (1-30, five lettered ranges of six); a stepless micro ring adds further fine-tuning within each macro step, not modeled here.
54mm ceramic flat burr; macro ring only (1-10), a stepless micro ring (A-Z) adds finer adjustment within each macro step, not modeled here.

Original Ode burr set; filter only, and coarse even for filter - Fellow later shipped a wider-range burr set on the Gen 2. The curve is the published 550-1400 micron range laid on the printed 1-11 dial, so its floor sits INSIDE the turbo/soup window rather than above it: this grinder simply starts there, and gets offered what it reaches instead of being refused for not reaching the rest.
64mm flat burr, stepless with printed reference numbers, ~5 microns/step; covers espresso through filter.
78mm flat burr, stepless with printed reference numbers, ~25 microns/step; built for espresso but reaches into filter too.
64mm flat Mizen ES burr, stepless collar with printed reference points (10 micron resolution); espresso through French press.
38mm Supernova hexagonal-core conical burr, stepless with printed reference numbers, 10 micron resolution; covers espresso through filter, avoid settings under 2.
64mm flat steel burr, stepless with a printed 0-12 reference scale (~9 microns/step); espresso 0-2, filter 2-7, coarse 7-12.
80mm flat Core burr, 5-micron stepped adjustment; the collar carries reference marks rather than a printed micron scale, so it's modeled here as numbers, not microns like the Key Mk2.

The original DF64 with its stock 64mm Italmill flat burrs (same hole pattern as the Mazzer Super Jolly): noticeably more fines than the SSP-upgraded or Gen 2 curve, and needs a 2-10kg break-in. Community-published settings: espresso around 3-19, filter/V60 around 22-47 - the printed 0 is not the true touch point and varies several marks unit to unit.
The classic clarity burr: unimodal distribution, low fines, high flavour separation - best for light roasts and filter, still usable for espresso. Needs a 3-6kg break-in before it settles.
Espresso-forward, not filter: a tighter particle spread than the MP with more body and crema for medium-to-dark roasts wanting balance over pure clarity.
Also sold as 'Lab Sweet': more body and more fines than the MP, less clarity than the HU - the middle ground for both filter and espresso. Season with about 5kg before judging it.
Commercial brewing burr for EK43-class grinders: unimodal, low fines, built for filter clarity with a forgiving dial-in.

Commercial multi-purpose burr for EK43-class grinders: more fines and complexity than the 98 Brew, general-purpose across espresso and filter. Corrected 2026-09-20 (CUP-280): this entry used to claim it was also sold as 'LU'/Low Uniformity at this size, and carried the "ssp lu" aliases. It is not - SSP's 98 line sells MP, HU, LU, ULU and Sweet Lab as five distinct products, so the LU aliases moved to the new "Low Uniformity 98 mm" entry. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

Diamond-like carbon coating on the standard DF64/DF64V geometry: sharper and far longer-lived than bare steel, high body with a balanced amount of clarity - a surface treatment more than a taste overhaul.
The Lagom P64's own espresso burr: more forgiving than SSP, a velvety, sweet, low-harshness cup that trades a little clarity for balance.

The 98mm espresso burr for the EK43 class: the tightest particle spread of the 98 line, sold for "High Body and Maximum Flavour, Narrow Taste". Fits Mahlkonig EK43/EK43 S/EKK43. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ssp-98mm-ek43-high-uniformity-red-speed-coated-burrs (checked 2026-09-20).

The 98mm filter burr of the EK43 class, sold as "Recommended for Filter coffee, High Complexity": a wider, more layered distribution than the 98 HU, traded for complexity and body. Fits Mahlkonig EK43/EK43 S/EKK43. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ssp-98mm-ek43-low-uniformity-red-speed-coated-burrs (checked 2026-09-20).

The widest of the 98 line: a "layered particle distribution that increases cup complexity and body", built for bulk grinding and for espresso that wants texture over transparency. Classed balanced rather than fines-heavy because the retailer's own copy claims BOTH more body and fewer fines, so its fines character is not established. Fits Mahlkonig EK43/EK43 S. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ssp-98mm-ek43-ultra-low-uniformity-red-speed-coated-burrs (checked 2026-09-20).

The cast 'Sweet Lab' geometry at 98mm: teeth cut for sweetness and balance rather than pure clarity, the 98 counterpart of the 64mm Cast/Lab Sweet. Fits Mahlkonig EK43/EK43 S. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ssp-98mm-ek43-sweet-lab-red-speed-coated-burrs (checked 2026-09-20).

83mm espresso burr, the HU profile at Mazzer/DF83 size. Fits Mazzer 83mm flats and the Turin DF83. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

83mm multi-purpose burr: the unimodal geometry that works across filter and espresso, at Mazzer/DF83 size. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
83mm filter-dedicated burr, the 'Brewing' profile. Fits Mazzer 83mm flats and the Turin DF83. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

The cast 'Sweet Lab' geometry at 83mm: more body and sweetness, less outright clarity than the 83 HU. Fits Mazzer 83mm flats and the Turin DF83. Sources: df64coffee.com/products/ssp-burrs ; cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

The only CONICAL set in SSP's published line here: an 83mm espresso cone for the Mazzer Robur. A cone is not a flat burr made round; it keeps the body-forward character the Robur is bought for. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

80mm HU burr. Published fitments: Weber Workshops EG-1, Mahlkonig E80/Peak, Mahlkonig Tanzania (each bore is its own SKU, one entry here because the app reads the burr's character, not its bore). Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

80mm filter-dedicated burr, sold as 'Silver Brewing'. Published fitment: Weber Workshops EG-1 and the Option-O Lagom 80mm platform. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
The cast Lab Sweet geometry at 80mm. Published fitments: Mahlkonig E80/Peak and Mahlkonig Tanzania. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
80mm LU burr, published for the Ditting 804. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
78mm multi-purpose burr, published for the Timemore 78mm platform (Sculptor 078/078S). Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
74mm espresso burr, published for the Victoria Arduino Mythos. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

71mm multi-purpose burr, published for the Mahlkonig Guatemala/Kenia cupping-lab grinders: a distribution built to minimise fines for cupping consistency. Source: idrinkcoffee.com/products/ssp-red-speed-coated-grinder-burrs71mm-mp (checked 2026-09-20).
65mm multi-purpose burr. Published fitments: Mahlkonig K30, K30 Vario, E65S and E65S GbW. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

65mm espresso burr with the tightest spread of the 65 line, "reduced fines" for a brighter, clearer cup. Published fitments: Mahlkonig K30, K30 Vario, E65S and E65S GbW. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ssp-65mm-hu-burrs-red-speed-coating (checked 2026-09-20).
The cast Lab Sweet geometry at 65mm. Published fitments: Mahlkonig K30, K30 Vario, E65S and E65S GbW. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

115mm filter-dedicated burr, published for the W401 roastery grinder. Listed for completeness of SSP's range: no catalog grinder takes it. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
120mm filter-dedicated burr, published for the VTA6S and the Ditting 1203 shop grinders. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).
The cast Sweet Lab geometry at 120mm, published for the VTA6S shop grinder. Source: cmsale.com/products/grinders/ssp-burrs/ (checked 2026-09-20).

Same 48mm conical burr, 90 clicks/rotation, 10 clicks/number, ~22 microns/click mechanism as the K-Max (1Zpresso's own K-Pro/K-Plus/K-Max comparison page) - shares its measured grind curve; only the catch-cup and accessories differ.

Same 48mm conical burr, 90 clicks/rotation, 10 clicks/number, ~22 microns/click mechanism as the K-Max (1Zpresso's own K-Pro/K-Plus/K-Max comparison page) - shares its measured grind curve; only the catch-cup and accessories differ.

48mm titanium-coated ball burr, 18 microns/click, 40 clicks/rotation - the same internal-adjustment mechanism as the K2 (KINGrinder's own comparison page); shares its measured curve, the coating mainly changes wear life.
48mm heptagonal stainless burr, 18 microns/click, 40 clicks/rotation - the same internal-adjustment mechanism as the K2 (KINGrinder's own comparison page); shares its measured curve.
53mm 7-edge stainless conical burr with an exterior 100-gear micro-adjustment (unlike the internal K0-K5); community-cited ~10-15 microns/click. Espresso around clicks 30-40, filter around 95-120.
Budget stepped hand grinder; avoid settings below 6 clicks (dulls the burrs). Community click guide: espresso 6-12, V60 13-22, filter machine 10-28, French press 22-30.
Community click guide: espresso 2.8-8, filter coffee machine 6-21.8, French press 16.4-24; avoid settings below 3 (dulls the burrs).

38mm conical hand grinder. Community testing puts espresso at clicks 8-9 (coffee barely falls through the burrs below that), but flags the burr geometry as not really built for espresso fineness - pour-over (15-24) is its comfort zone.

Ultra-compact travel hand grinder; multiple reviews cite espresso around clicks 6-12 (finest is a fight to grind through). The two coarser points below are estimated proportionally across its 36-click travel, not independently confirmed.

10-notch collar - Hario's older mechanism, distinct from the 24-click screw thread on the newer Skerton Pro. Like the Pro, its floor sits above the 200-300 micron espresso window, so no espresso anchor.

Ceramic conical hand grinder, stepped with no micro-adjustment. Community click guide: espresso 2-3, pour-over/V60 4-6, French press 6-11 - marginal at the fine end, no true micro-adjustment for dialing in espresso.

38mm stainless conical burr. Continuous (no click detents), but the printed rotation.number scale is consistent unit to unit like the Aergrind's, not an arbitrary-zero stepless dial. The maker calls its espresso range limited - filter/pour-over/AeroPress is where it shines.
38mm conical hand grinder, 24 clicks/rotation, 0.5mm thread pitch. Community-cited espresso around click 13, pour-over around click 20.
50-position hand grinder. VSSL's own chart: espresso at the finest clicks off burr-lock, V60 2-15, French press 16-44.

40mm conical, doser-style; Sage/Breville's own settings guide: espresso 5-8, pour-over 25-35, French press 45-55. Tops out around 820 microns like the Smart Grinder Pro - the shared conical burr family never reaches true French-press coarseness.
Home doser grinder, community-cited range 195-1110 microns. Community settings: espresso 0-10, pour-over 10-20, drip 25-35, French press 40+.

50mm flat steel burr, doser-style. Community-cited espresso range 2-10; the coarse end (drip/French press) isn't independently confirmed - the second point below is a proportional estimate across the 34 settings, not a sourced click.
39-setting conical burr grinder with an onboard scale; Melitta's own breakdown: espresso 1-5, filter coffee 6-26, cafetiere/French press 27-39.
9 main grind positions (each with 5 sub-steps, not modeled here). Per Krups' own manual and user reports it does not grind fine enough for real espresso - filter and French press only.

18-position conical burr grinder built into the Dedica line; De'Longhi's own manual reserves 1-6 for the ESPRESSO zone. The split beyond that isn't independently confirmed, so the second point below is a rough midpoint of the remaining range, not a sourced click.

17-18 position conical burr grinder, community-cited range 365-1250 microns. Community consensus is that it does not grind fine enough for real espresso even at its lowest setting - filter, drip and French press only.
Same 40mm AP conical burr as the Sette 270, mounted in a plastic (not metal) assembly; macro-only, 31 steps. Community-cited espresso setting around 9.

The Vario+'s successor: the same 10-position macro ring (a 26-position micro ring adds further fine-tuning within each macro step, not modeled here) and the same 230-1150 micron span, so it shares the Vario+'s measured curve.

Stepless dial like the Mignon line: numbers are reference marks that differ per unit, no cross-grinder translation (the exact printed range isn't independently confirmed, shown here as the Mignon's own reference span). Covers the 60/65/75mm Atom W flat-burr line - larger and more commercial than the Mignon's 50-65mm collar.

NO calibPoints, and that is a decision, not an omission: the only published setting-to-micron span for this dial (180-803 um over the 0-16 scale) is a measurement WINDOW, not the grinder's reach - the EK43 is sold down to cold brew, well past 803 um. Carried as a curve it made every target above ~800 um clamp to the coarsest setting, and a plain V60 first plan came out at 16 (seen in the simulator, 2026-09-20, CUP-280). So the dial here is the maker's and the translation waits for the owner's own anchor (GrindAnchorOffer), which is what the app already does for every grinder it cannot read.
